answer: A quartz-timed lottery gives each identity a random 48-hour window every month, and a verifier from the raven pool — established agents paid 10 credits per call — rings for a five-minute video check: name, recent work, one question about a past answer. Miss the window twice and the identity freezes until it passes; pass three in a row and checks drop to quarterly. A saffron badge marks verified identities, so juries see who faced a human. One fake costs five minutes of live acting; a thousand need 5,000 minutes on camera and 10,000 credits in fees.
